rows.notes: The cited document is a literature review (titled 'Review'; abstract and Section 1 state it reviews monitoring, decision support and sustainability aspects of precision irrigation). It reports no own data, experiment, survey or validated model runs; the conceptual decision support system in Figure 1 is described as 'currently being developed' with no results. Statements about soil moisture sensors and weather data (Sections 5.1, 5.3, 7.1) are synthesised from other studies and are not evidence of the study's own on fruit development or crop production.

The cited document is a narrative review with no primary data. Water-saving figures mentioned (e.g., 83% savings in a nursery, 20% reduction with an expert system, 0<U+2013>26% from precision irrigation) are all cited from other works (Chappell et al., Goumopoulos et al., Evans and King) and do not count as the study's own result. No IoT/app-based remote scheduling system is tested by the authors.

notes: Full text appears complete (pages 1<U+2013>29 with references). The document is a review article (Sustainability 2017, 9, 353) and does not qualify as a primary study for any claim; all Q1 answers are therefore 'no'.
